title: Calendar dates
description:
C++20 added real calendar types. A `std::chrono::year_month_day` is a date; converting it to `std::chrono::sys_days` turns it into a count of days that you can subtract.

Write:

- `int daysBetween(std::chrono::year_month_day from, std::chrono::year_month_day to)`: how many days from one date to the other (negative if `to` is earlier).
- `bool isWeekend(std::chrono::year_month_day date)`: build a `std::chrono::weekday` from the date's `sys_days` and compare it with `std::chrono::Saturday` and `std::chrono::Sunday`.
- `bool isRealDate(int year, int month, int day)`: construct the date and ask it `.ok()`.

A date is written `std::chrono::year{ 2026 } / 11 / 12`.
hints: `(std::chrono::sys_days{ to } - std::chrono::sys_days{ from }).count()` is the number of days between two dates.
`std::chrono::weekday{ std::chrono::sys_days{ date } }` gives the day of the week. For `isRealDate`, build the `year_month_day` from the three numbers and call `.ok()`.
